framework.assumption: Standard .NET 10 framework API contract, not verification of an installed reference pack or external compiler inputs. Future/replacement surfaces outside this model are unsupported.

provenance.commitVerification: Declared commits; scanner byte hashes and separate evaluator hashes identify the measured code.

policy.unit: one file × CWE × polarity, except declared multi-file suffix variants (22a/b, 51, 52, 53, 54, 61, 66, 67, 68, 71, 72, 73, 74, 75, 81), which count once per family, variant, CWE, and polarity (including 81 bad/good split)
policy.match: open finding with exact CWE and path, with its start line inside a labeled Bad/Good method or explicitly named bad/good class region in any file in the unit
limitations: Ground-truth regions use Juliet C# method names beginning Bad/Good and explicitly named bad/good class files; 81 base/helper files are included in source hashing and scanning but are not polarity labels.
The public NIST archive does not include a standalone manifest; the archive hash and generated label hash are recorded, and file names plus labeled source regions determine the units.
This benchmark is synthetic third-party test code, not independent ASP.NET application evidence or a measure of production false-positive rates.

focusedInjection.interpretation: Affected diagnostic categories, not all supported CWEs; full-suite totals retain every CWE

confidenceStrata.reason: Frozen benchmark matches omit per-finding confidence; do not infer medium+ or high counts.

policy.match: exact source path and expected CWE in finding.cwe; status=open

policy.unit: one manifest testcase × CWE × bad/good polarity; methods and helper classes are aggregated
policy.match: open finding with exact CWE and path, with its start line inside a labeled method/class region (or exact manifest flaw line when no method encloses it)
limitations: Manifest flaw labels anchor bad regions. Good regions require explicit Juliet good method/class naming; missing good regions never create a negative.

The official 1.3 manifest contains redundant closing testcase tags and cases without flaw entries. Redundant closings are counted and ignored; missing-flaw cases use the explicit CWE filename plus bad/good naming convention and remain in the denominator.

For the exact official 1.3 manifest hash only, an anchor conflicting with an explicitly good region is recorded and the suite good/bad convention takes precedence. This is corrected-label scoring, not pristine manifest scoring.
All good variants, wrappers, and helpers in a testcase form one negative unit. One matching detection anywhere predicts the aggregate positive; this is not per-method or per-flaw accuracy.
Neutral methods enclosing manifest flaws are bad regions. Other neutral helper methods, main/support code, and unlabeled source regions are unscored.
Separate good/bad helper classes use their complete original file regions. No target source is rewritten and scanner taint analysis still sees coexisting good/bad methods.
No call-graph reachability or cross-file taint is added by the evaluator; an intra-method or helper-class detection can satisfy its testcase unit.

policy.unit: one explicit SARIF result location × CWE × polarity
policy.match: open finding with exact source path and CWE and start line at the labeled line, or within an explicitly supplied inclusive upstream line range
limitations: A bad/good run state labels its explicit result locations; mixed runs require an explicit result kind fail/pass or properties.state bad/good. Missing or conflicting metadata is rejected.
No safe locations are inferred from absent results. Datasets with only bad labels have no negative denominator and FPR is n/a.
Exact labeled locations can miss a valid detection reported at a nearby source or sink; no line tolerance, CWE aliases, or file-level fallback is applied.
Artifacts are checked against supplied byte length and SHA-256; declared hashes and computed hashes are retained in JSON. Other hash algorithms are preserved but not verified.
URI base IDs, remote/absolute URIs, parent traversal, symbolic links, ambiguous artifacts, duplicate labels, and missing labeled files are rejected.

policy.match: open finding in a listed affected file with exact expected CWE; duplicates count once
policy.fixLabel: negative for the cited CWE in selected affected files only
policy.context: full selected source files, limited repository context; not CVE localization or application-wide safety
policy.provenance: first parent verified during curation; immutable source bytes verified offline on every run

policy.match: open vulnerability finding within reviewed inclusive source region; exact advisory CWE and permitted rule/evidence criteria
policy.parentLabel: positive for the cited fix-specific mechanism
policy.fixLabel: negative for the cited fix-specific mechanism
policy.context: source localization is a static benchmark proxy; does not prove exploitability or application safety
